decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 166158, so no exact-duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe pass is required.

year, month, day, carrier, flight, and sched_dep_time are all null_rate 0.0 and together identify a single scheduled flight record; tailnum and dep_time were excluded from the grain because they carry nulls (0.009154 and 0.029388 respectively).
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all marked is_airbyte_metadata true and describe the capture tool, not the flight, so all three are dropped.

dep_time (null_rate 0.029388), arr_time (null_rate 0.0307), dep_delay and arr_delay (null_rates 0.029388 and 0.032981) and air_time (null_rate 0.032981) are retained as nullable rather than imputed, consistent with cancelled or diverted flights.
tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 of 166158 rows), likely reflecting unmatched aircraft registrations, so it is retained as a nullable VARCHAR rather than required.
time_hour samples are consistently ISO-8601 UTC strings (e.g. 2013-01-01T10:00:00Z) with null_rate 0.0, supporting a strict cast to TIMESTAMP.

purpose: This table provides a cleaned, typed view of the 2013 NYC flights departure and arrival records landed from bronze.nyc_flights, intended as the analytics-ready base for on-time performance and scheduling analyses.
usage: Consumers should expect INTEGER time and delay fields in raw HHMM or minute-delta form (not true time-of-day types) and should treat null dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, air_time, or tailnum values as cancelled, diverted, or otherwise unmatched flights rather than missing data to be imputed.
limitations: Delay and timing fields (dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, air_time) retain null rates between roughly 2.9% and 3.3%, and tailnum retains a 0.9% null rate; none of these were imputed or dropped, so downstream aggregates must explicitly handle nulls. Exact duplicate rows were checked and found absent (duplicate_row_rate 0.0), so no row-level dedupe logic is applied.
